newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire to let its envoy stand trial in France.
newsitem.headline: Zaire to let its envoy stand trial in France.

text.p: Zaire will let France try its ambassador to Paris, whose car ran over two schoolboys in the Riviera town of Menton, an aide to President Mobutu Sese Seko said on Tuesday.

Police say Ambassador Ramazani Baya was driving at 100 kph (60 mph) in a 45-kph (30-mph) zone when his car hit the two boys on a pedestrian crossing. Raphael Lenoir, 13, was killed instantly and Ronald Lehartel, 12, died on Saturday after a prolonged coma.

"The president of the republic has assured the mayor of Menton that he will make sure that the Zairean government grants the request for the lifting of Ambassador Ramazani Baya's diplomatic immunity," Mobutu aide Atumba Ngbanda said.

Ngbanda said Baya had informed Mobutu that he would ask Kinshasa to lift his immunity so that he could stand trial in France in connection with the deaths of the boys, who were run over by Baya's car in the Riviera resort on November 23.

The announcement ended a diplomatic tug-of-war between Paris and Kinshasa over the envoy's status after the French Foreign Ministry demanded that Baya be withdrawn and urged that he be brought to justice in France.

The incident has embarrassed France as well as Zaire by putting the focus on the presence of Mobutu, a pariah banned from much of Europe and the United States, in his palatial Riviera mansion during a crisis over hundreds of thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire.
The Zairean leader has been holed up at at his villa in the Riviera town of Roquebrune-Cap-Martin while convalescing from prostate cancer surgery.
After initially playing down the accident as something that could happen to anyone, the French Foreign Ministry had hardened its tone, demanding that Baya be brought to justice.

"We're obviously pushing very hard on this matter because it is a question of justice and respect for the families," French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette had told the National Assembly during parliamentary questioning earlier on Tuesday.
Mobutu announced his decision in the case after meeting the mayor of Menton and members of the dead boys' families at his Riviera villa.
Baya has written to the boys' families expressing remorse.
An official at the Zairean Embassy in Paris said Baya was still in France but would leave after carrying out unspecified formalities at the embassy and at the French Foreign Ministry.

The Foreign Ministry, which on Monday asked Zaire to allow Baya to stand trial for the deaths, said it expected the envoy to return to Zaire for consultations before returning to France to stand trial.
